correctness.rationale: Fixed simplices in the ordinary discrete Morse graph complex are equivariant acyclic partial successor functions. Orbit divisibility determines possible targets and weights. Directed cycles in the quotient occur if and only if in the original successor function: around a quotient cycle all orbit sizes agree, and the composition is a finite cyclic shift. The action sign of an arrow orbit of size d is (-1)^(d-1); the directed matrix-forest determinant therefore reproduces every graded chain trace. Substitution t=-1 gives the reduced Lefschetz determinant. Equal-length complete-graph blocks have eigenvalues stated in RESULT.md. The standalone exact rational script enumerated all 293 graph-automorphism pairs through four vertices, all complete-graph permutation cycle products through six, and three six-vertex graded instances. These are checks, not a substitute for the symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: Material comparison distinguishes identity-action Laplacian enumerations, general fixed-simplex Lefschetz formulas, and complete-graph orbit homology dimensions from the new all-graph, automorphism-specific full graded chain character. The signed orbit-divisibility quotient and universal determinant are not statements/implications established in the inspected primary works. Search results found a special complete-bipartite involution character, already a proper special case rather than the uniform theorem. The inaccessible full text of a contemporary strong-Morse paper and possible unindexed equivalent forest formulas remain explicit risks.
residual_risks: The complete 2026 Knudson–Owens-White manuscript was not materially read; its accessible abstract contrasts strong with ordinary matchings and does not establish the claimed all-graph formula, but an incidental equivariant observation cannot be excluded.
An unindexed equivariant matrix-forest or directed-forest representation theorem may give an equivalent expression; semantic and direct-literature searches are not exhaustive novelty certification.
An earlier computation for the bipartition-exchange involution of K_{m,m} is a proper special case; the special case is not claimed as new.

value.rationale: The full graded character of the natural automorphism action on the graph Morse complex is a motivated topological representation invariant. The arbitrary-graph theorem reduces an exponential face enumeration to a determinant of size equal to the number of vertex orbits, retaining subtle simplex orientation signs. The closed complete-graph factorization computes all S_n conjugacy-class graded characters uniformly in n; neither the ordinary identity-action forest polynomial nor a special graph trace provides this invariant. The theorem is a structural extension useful for Lefschetz fixed-point and symmetry analysis, rather than a small finite recomputation. It does not assert that an arbitrary homology representation is recovered degree by degree.
